title: Test Gap: Add assertions to warm vs cold boot snapshot comparison test
author: Ryangwaite
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the test gap

An assertion mechanism needs to be added to the `test_warmboot_data_consistency` test. Currently, any inconsistencies that are found are log warned out but the test does not fail.

The challenges with doing this are:
- There are currently inconsistencies, but these should not cause the test to fail so how can we ignore them safely?
- How can we handle the variations in inconsistencies version-to-version and platform-to-platform?
- How can new inconsistencies cause the test to fail only?
- How can fixed inconsistencies that are still ignored by signaled to us? Fail the test?
- How can we enforce that consistency improves over time and things aren't ignored forever?

### Affected Area

tests/upgrade_path/test_warmboot_data_consistency.py

### Impact of missing tests and proposed tests

Currently the test output needs to be manually inspected. With these new assertions in place manual effort is eliminated and the quality improves too.

Summary:
Fixes #21226
MSFT ADO: 38503975

Added assertions and an assertion mask framework for the warmboot data consistency test to validate Arista devices automatically. This enables detection of unexpected differences during warm-vs-cold boot comparisons.

Note the assertion mask is currently set to cold 202511.29 vs 202505.30--wb-->202511.29 Arista mask. Any failures on 202605 will be handled in follow-up PRs. 

For platforms without an assertion mask, those tests continue to pass and require manual review of differences to assess if there is an issue.

### Type of change

<!--
- Fill x for your type of change.
- e.g.
- [x] Bug fix
-->

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
    - [ ] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [x] Test case improvement


### Back port request
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [ ] 202512
- [x] 202605

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
Without this change the test doesn't have any assertions and requires manual effort to look through the diff which is time consuming. With this change, now for the 3 Arista platforms, their changes are assessed against a set of vetted and known diffs. If a new diff is found the test will fail and only at that point will the manual effort be required.

#### How did you do it?
1. Created a new `warm_vs_cold_assertion_mask.py` module that provides a declarative framework for masking expected post-prune diffs on a per-platform, per-upgrade-path basis
2. Enhanced `db_comparison.py` with expanded comparison logic and utilities
3. Extended `snapshot_warm_vs_cold_boot_helpers.py` to support the new assertion framework
4. Updated `warm_vs_cold.py` with assertion mask application logic
5. Modified `test_warmboot_data_consistency.py` to apply the assertion mask and assert no unmasked regressions remain
6. Added helper utilities in `dut_utils.py` to support the test improvements

#### How did you verify/test it?
**202605 sonic-mgmt branch**
Tested cold 202511.29 vs 202505.30--wb-->202511.29 on Arista:
- Arista-7050CX3-32S-C32
- Arista-7260CX3-D108C8
- Arista-7060CX-32S-D48C8

#### Any platform specific information?
This lays the assertion framework but only enables it for the following platforms:
- x86_64-arista_7260
- x86_64-arista_7060
- x86_64-arista_7050cx3

Other platforms continue to have their current functionality

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?
Still T0*

comments.author: Ryangwaite
comments.body:
> @Ryangwaite — ❌ The assertion framework needs two correctness fixes before merge.
> 
> **Template**: ✅ Complete **DCO / CLA**: ✅ Passed **CI**: ✅ All reported checks passed
> 
> **Code Review:**
> 
> 1. **[Important] Scope the assertion mask by upgrade path.** `warm_vs_cold_assertion_mask.py` describes masks as platform-and-upgrade-path specific, and this mask was validated for 202505 → 202511, but `resolve_warm_cold_diff_mask()` selects only by platform and `test_warmboot_data_consistency.py` passes only `duthost.facts["platform"]`. Consequently, another path such as 202511 → 202605 on the same Arista platform will reuse exclusions that were never vetted for that path, potentially masking a real regression. Please include the base/target release in mask selection.
> 2. **[Important] Support valid ECMP widths in the route-weight expectation.** The mask accepts only `"1"` and `"1,1,1,1"`, but SONiC also produces valid values such as `"1,1"` for two-member ECMP. Those routes will remain unmasked and fail an otherwise clean test. Please match an arbitrary all-ones ECMP list, for example `ValueSpec.regex(r"1(,1)*")`, rather than hard-coding one- and four-member cases.
> 
> Please address these before merge.

Hi Storm,

1. This is intentional to have it only passing on 202505 → 202511 for now. This locks in our expectations for the 202511 release. It will then be run against 202511->202605 and any failures are an image regression. At that point we must assess if they are accepted image regressions or an image change is needed. I don't want to blindly allow them through in the test now as it risks hiding image issues. There will be a follow-up PR to address allowed and vetted 202605 changes.

2. Have addressed this in commit 5a94bfad5d11. Thanks
